notes.content: The page arranges six relations in an implication diagram (1.18), initially calls four of them order relations, distinguishes the two symmetric relations, and gives the empty-figure criterion for self-parallelism (1.19). Remark a) explains recovery of incidence from the order using strict irreducibles (1.20), then recovery of the distinguished family, deployment and order from incidence in (1.21), (1.22), and the literally comma-numbered (1,23). The final sentence about data fixing the atelier structure continues off the page.
notes.math_reading_decisions: Five implication arrows point downward. The enclosure has two left-corner gaps. The dark compatibility sign includes an uncertain extra upright; the two cleaner body signs are open opposed zigzags. The marginal proposed definition repeats F in all variable positions; no G is supplied. Formula (1.22) literally ends in the family F glyph, even though the preceding prose names an ordinary F. Tildes are waves, the final inclusion is open with no lower bar, and the index under Sup and both F subscripts in (1.20) are i; the quantified variable after the existential sign is also i. H’s note about the retraced last inequality is credited; no recoverable canceled operand was found there.
author_doubts: Non, $\triangleleft$ n’est pas rel. d’ordre, elle est transitive mais non réflexive, car $F\triangleleft F\Longleftrightarrow F\unsure{\in|\overset{\prime}{\in}}\unsure{\mathcal{M}|M}$
Pour avoir une relation d’ordre il faudrait écrire $F\trianglelefteq F\overset{\mathrm{déf}}{\Longleftrightarrow}F\triangleleft F$ ou $F=F$.
notes.titles_dates_counts: Own page number 11; underlined Remarques with a); display labels (1.18), (1.19), (1.20), (1.21), (1.22), (1,23); internal reference (1.17). No date, title sheet, archive pencil number or page-count declaration is visible.
